title: Scottish Music 2
description: Revise Scottish Music concepts introduced up to National 5, including instruments and features used in related Celtic music.

items.prompt: As a keyboard instrument, pressing a key causes a felt-covered hammer to strike a string.
Name the specific Scottish social-dance ensemble commonly featuring accordion, fiddle, piano, bass and drum kit.
The sound made when a person sings or speaks.
A Scottish Gaelic vocal style, also called puirt-a-beul, using rhythmic Gaelic or nonsense syllables.
Give the general Scots-language narrative folk-song category, rather than a particular farm-worker or cloth-working song tradition.
An accompaniment holds or repeats one note or a fifth beneath a melody, without a sequence of changing chords. Name the accompaniment.
Name the general term for a decorative note or group added to a melody, rather than one particular type of decoration.
A scale made from five different notes within the octave.
A repeated accompaniment pattern, often alternating a bass note on the beat with a chord off the beat.
Name the general rhythmic feature created by adding half of a note’s written value with a dot, often producing unequal long-short or short-long pairs.
A lively Scottish or Irish dance in compound time, often 6/8.
A short accented note followed by a longer note, often written as a semiquaver followed by a dotted quaver.
